subject: history_social
notes: The first transcontinental railroad in the United States was completed in May 1869 at Promontory Summit, Utah.
The Central Pacific Railroad built the line eastward from Sacramento, California, through the Sierra Nevada.
At the peak of construction, Chinese immigrants made up as much as 90 percent of the Central Pacific's workforce.
They blasted tunnels through granite and worked through severe mountain winters.
In the best-known photograph of the completion ceremony, no Chinese workers can be identified.
stem: The student wants to emphasize the contrast between Chinese workers' contribution to the railroad and their absence from the way its completion was recorded. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Chinese immigrants, as much as 90 percent of the Central Pacific's workforce at its peak, blasted tunnels through granite and worked through harsh winters.
choices.B: Building eastward from Sacramento through the Sierra Nevada, the Central Pacific met its partner line at Promontory Summit, Utah, in May 1869.
choices.C: The best-known photograph of the 1869 ceremony at Promontory Summit, Utah, which marked the railroad's completion, shows no identifiable Chinese workers.
choices.D: Although Chinese immigrants made up as much as 90 percent of the Central Pacific's workforce, none can be identified in the best-known photo of its completion.

explanation.why: The goal requires both sides of a contrast: how much Chinese workers contributed (as much as 90 percent of the workforce) and how they were left out of the record (absent from the best-known photograph). Only one choice joins the two with "Although."
explanation.A: Incorrect. It emphasizes the workers' contribution but says nothing about their absence from the record.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It describes the railroad's route and completion without mentioning the Chinese workers at all.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It describes the absence from the photograph but not the scale of the workers' contribution, so the contrast is lost.
explanation.D: Correct. It sets the workers' large share of the workforce against their absence from the best-known photograph.
